## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paccavekkhaṇa Sutta* (Ud 6.3; PTS Ud 66) is the third discourse of the sixth chapter of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. In this text, the Buddha reflects upon the unskillful qualities that he has abandoned [SuttaCentral].
In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies an internal Pali match with the *Papañcakhaya Sutta* (Ud 7.7), sharing formulaic narrative segments (§0.2–2.1) [DharmaNexus]. According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels to the verse are found in the *Nirvāṇavarga* of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 26) and its Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 26), as well as in Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* traditions (T 210.36, T 212.27, and T 213.26) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies resembling parallels in the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 228), the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 224–242), the Patna *Dharmapada* (P-Dhp 278–305), and other parallel collections including UV 29 and T 210.25 [SuttaCentral].
None of the secondary literature passages surveyed address this particular discourse directly; they instead examine the general Buddhist doctrinal and epistemological concept of reviewing or introspection (*paccavekkhaṇa* / *paccavekkhaṇañāṇa*), or discuss other suttas dealing with reflection such as the *Ambalaṭṭhikārāhulovāda Sutta* (MN 61) and *Anumāna Sutta* (MN 15).
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
